doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: How many lyric songs by 1964; The Word From Mose
summary: Amy and Audre sort out when he became fully a singer-songwriter on Atlantic.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So in 1964, when you go to London, about how many songs had you written? Perhaps Amy can tell me that.
Are you talking about with lyrics?
Oh my God. I don’t know. Like...
Here. But it doesn’t have the dates.
The first, I think, I Don’t Worry About A Thing, was an album that had a mix, like half-and-half. I feel like that was the album where you did more, the first one where you...
Well, that’s not true. Columbia had some that...
Well, I wrote some of them, and I don’t know...
By 1964, he’d probably a lot of ones with lyrics, I think. What do you think, Mom?
I think so. I don’t know how many albums were...
By the time Word For Mose came, that was all vocals. Wasn’t it? Word For Mose. That was like ‘64 or ‘65. But before then, it was always half...
Yes. I think that was your first record for Atlantic, if I’m not mistaken. So for Atlantic is when you started presenting yourself fully as a singer and songwriter, it sounds like.
